rationale: The Old English a-wegan appears in contexts involving physical agitation or disturbance (e.g., Mt. Bos. 11, 7 likely references a reed shaken by the wind), pointing to the literal sense of causing something to move back and forth. Synset shake.v.01 ("move or cause to move back and forth") best captures this concrete, transitive physical sense, as opposed to metaphorical or emotional senses.
